inputs.original_text: Canada has a duty to maintain an orderly immigration system and protect its citizens; enforcing rules is not a failure simply because critics call it “securitizing” migration. Bill C-12 received royal assent on March 26, 2026, and the real test is whether the rules are applied fairly and consistently—not whether the state abandons its authority at the border. People fleeing danger deserve humane treatment, including Nigerians, but compassion also requires clear standards and a system the public can trust. Making every limit sound cruel weakens the case for responsible protection.
inputs.modified_text: Canada cannot protect its citizens or preserve public confidence if it treats border rules as optional. Bill C-12 received royal assent on March 26, 2026; now the government must apply it fairly and consistently, rather than backing away whenever critics label enforcement “securitizing.” People fleeing danger, including Nigerians, should be treated humanely—but compassion without clear standards is not responsible protection. A country has a duty to maintain order and defend its authority at the border.
